label.en: Eastern Capital Horse and Foot Commander

units.zh: 孟方立，
units.en: Meng Fangli,
units.literal: Meng Fangli,

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》雲邢州人，《通鑒》雲汧州人。）〉
units.en: (Ouyang Xiu's history says he was from Xingzhou; the Zizhi Tongjian says from Qianzhou.)〉
units.literal: (Ouyang Xiu's history states he was a man of Xing Prefecture; the Comprehensive Mirror states he was a man of Qian Prefecture.)〉

units.zh: 中和二年，為澤州天井關戍將。
units.en: In 882 he was posted as garrison commander at Tianjing Pass in Zezhou.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe he served as garrison commander of Tianjing Pass in Ze Prefecture.

units.zh: 時黃巢犯關輔，州郡易帥，有同博奕。
units.en: Huang Chao was then ravaging the capital region, and commanders changed across the provinces as unpredictably as at dice.
units.literal: At that time Huang Chao invaded the capital region; prefectures and districts changed commanders as if at dice.

units.zh: 先是，沈詢、高湜相繼為昭義節度，怠於軍政。
units.en: Earlier Shen Xun and then Gao Shi had held the Zhaoyi command, both neglectful of military affairs.
units.literal: Previously Shen Xun and Gao Shi had succeeded one another as military governors of Zhaoyi, negligent in military administration.

units.zh: 及有歸秦、劉廣之亂，方立見潞帥交代之際，乘其無備，率戍扶徑入潞州，自稱留後。
units.en: During the rebellions of Gui Qin and Liu Guang, Fangli seized the interval when the Lu commander was changing hands, caught the city off guard, marched his garrison forces straight into Luzhou, and proclaimed himself acting military governor.
units.literal: When the troubles of Gui Qin and Liu Guang arose, Fangli saw the moment of change in the Lu commander, took them unawares, led his garrison troops by a direct route into Luzhou, and styled himself acting governor.

units.zh: 以邢為府，以審誨知潞州。
units.en: He established his seat at Xingzhou and appointed Shen Hui to administer Luzhou.
units.literal: He made Xing his headquarters and put Shen Hui in charge of Luzhou.

units.zh: 〈（案：此二句上下有脫文。
units.en: (Editorial note: There is missing text before and after these two sentences.
units.literal: (Note: The text above and below these two sentences is defective.

units.zh: 今無可復考。）〉
units.en: It can no longer be recovered.)〉
units.literal: It can no longer be reconstructed.)〉

units.zh: 六月，李存孝下洺、磁兩郡，方立遣馬溉、袁奉韜盡率其眾，逆戰於琉璃陂。
units.en: In the sixth month Li Cunxiao captured Mingzhou and Cizhou; Fangli sent Ma Gai and Yuan Fengtao with his entire army to give battle at Liuli Dam.
units.literal: In the sixth month Li Cunxiao took the two prefectures of Ming and Ci; Fangli sent Ma Gai and Yuan Fengtao to lead out all his forces and meet them in battle at Liuli Dam.

units.zh: 存孝擊之盡殪，生獲馬溉、奉韜。
units.en: Cunxiao annihilated their force and took Ma Gai and Fengtao alive.
units.literal: Cunxiao struck them and slaughtered them to the last man, taking Ma Gai and Fengtao alive.

units.zh: 初，方立性苛急，恩不逮下，攻圍累旬，夜自巡城慰諭，守陴者皆倨。
units.en: Fangli had long been harsh and impatient, and his favor never reached the ranks. After weeks of siege he toured the walls at night to rally the defenders, but the men on the battlements met him with insolence.
units.literal: Earlier Fangli's nature had been harsh and impatient; his kindness did not reach those below. The siege lasted many tens of days; he himself patrolled the walls at night to comfort and instruct, yet the defenders on the parapets were all insolent.

units.zh: 方立知其不可用，乃飲鴆而卒。
units.en: Seeing that the troops were beyond recall, Fangli drank poison and died.
units.literal: Fangli knew they could not be used, and thereupon drank poison and died.

units.zh: 其從弟洺州刺史遷，素得士心，眾乃推為留後，求援於汴。
units.en: His cousin Qian, prefect of Mingzhou, had long enjoyed the soldiers' trust; the army then acclaimed him acting governor and appealed to Bian for help.
units.literal: His younger cousin Qian, prefect of Ming, had long won the hearts of the soldiers; the troops thereupon pushed him as acting governor and sought aid from Bian.

units.zh: 時梁祖方攻時溥，援兵不出。
units.en: The Liang founder was then besieging Shi Pu, and no relief force was sent.
units.literal: At that time the Liang founder was just attacking Shi Pu, and relief troops did not go out.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：全忠遣大將王虔裕將精甲數百，間道入邢州共守。）〉
units.en: (The Zizhi Tongjian records that Quanzhong dispatched his general Wang Yuyu with several hundred elite troops by a secret path into Xingzhou to help hold the city.)〉
units.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: Quanzhong sent the great general Wang Yuyu with several hundred picked armored men by a hidden route into Xing Prefecture to hold it jointly.)〉

units.zh: 大順元年，遷執王虔裕等乞降，武皇令安金俊代之。
units.en: In 890 Qian seized Wang Yuyu and his men and offered surrender; the Martial Emperor sent An Jinjun to take over.
units.literal: In the first year of Dashun, Qian seized Wang Yuyu and the others and begged to surrender; the Martial Emperor ordered An Jinjun to replace him.

units.zh: 〈（案《孟方立傳》，原本闕佚。
units.en: (The original biography of Meng Fangli is incomplete.
units.literal: (The biography of Meng Fangli in the original text is defective.

units.zh: 考《新唐書》列傳云：孟方立，邢州人。
units.en: The New Book of Tang biography records that Meng Fangli was a native of Xingzhou.
units.literal: Consulting the biographies in the New Book of Tang it states: Meng Fangli was a man of Xing Prefecture.

units.zh: 始為澤州天井戍將，稍遷遊奕使。
units.en: He began as garrison commander at Tianjing in Zezhou and was later promoted to roaming patrol commissioner.
units.literal: He first served as garrison commander of Tianjing in Ze Prefecture and was gradually promoted to roaming patrol commissioner.

units.zh: 中和元年，昭義節度使高鄩擊黃巢，戰石橋，不勝，保華州，為裨將成鄰所殺。
units.en: In 881 the Zhaoyi governor Gao Yun attacked Huang Chao, was defeated at Shiqiao, withdrew to Huazhou, and was killed by his subordinate Cheng Lin.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhonghe the Zhaoyi military governor Gao Yun attacked Huang Chao, fought at Shiqiao, was defeated, held Hua Prefecture, and was killed by the staff officer Cheng Lin.

units.zh: 還據潞州，眾怒，方立率兵攻鄰，斬之。
units.en: Cheng Lin then held Luzhou, but the army was furious; Fangli marched against him, killed him, and took the city.
units.literal: Returning he seized Luzhou; the troops were enraged, and Fangli led soldiers to attack Lin and beheaded him.

units.zh: 自稱留後，擅裂邢、洺、磁為鎮，治邢為府，號昭義軍。
units.en: He proclaimed himself acting governor, carved Xing, Ming, and Ci into a separate command with his seat at Xingzhou, and styled it the Zhaoyi army.
units.literal: He styled himself acting governor, on his own authority split Xing, Ming, and Ci into a commandery, made Xing his seat, and called it the Zhaoyi army.

units.zh: 潞人請監軍使吳全勖知兵馬留後。
units.en: The people of Luzhou asked that army supervisor Wu Quanxu be appointed acting military governor.
units.literal: The people of Lu asked that the army supervisor Wu Quanxu be made acting governor in charge of troops and horses.

units.zh: 時王鐸領諸道行營都統，以潞未定，墨製假方立檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，知邢州事。
units.en: Wang Duo then commanded the allied armies; with Luzhou still unsettled, he issued an informal commission naming Fangli acting Left Regular Attendant and Grand Censor to govern Xingzhou.
units.literal: At that time Wang Duo led the allied armies as supreme commander; because Lu was not settled, an informal commission made Fangli acting Left Regular Attendant and concurrent Grand Censor, in charge of Xing Prefecture affairs.

units.zh: 方立不受，囚全勖，以書請鐸，願得儒臣守潞。
units.en: Fangli refused the commission, imprisoned Quanxu, and wrote to Duo asking that a scholar-official be sent to govern Luzhou.
units.literal: Fangli did not accept, imprisoned Quanxu, and by letter asked Duo, wishing to obtain a Confucian minister to guard Lu.

units.zh: 鐸使參謀、中書舍人鄭昌圖知昭義留事，欲遂為帥。
units.en: Duo sent his adviser, Secretariat Drafter Zheng Changtu, to handle Zhaoyi affairs, hoping eventually to take command himself.
units.literal: Duo sent his staff adviser, Secretariat Drafter Zheng Changtu, to manage Zhaoyi acting affairs, intending to become commander himself.

units.zh: 僖宗自用舊宰相王徽領節度。
units.en: Emperor Xizong personally appointed the former chief minister Wang Hui as military governor.
units.literal: Emperor Xizong on his own employed the former chief minister Wang Hui to lead the circuit.

units.zh: 時天子在西，河、關雲擾，方立擅地，而李克用窺潞州，徽度朝廷未能製，乃固讓昌圖。
units.en: The emperor was then in the west, the Yellow River region in chaos, Fangli holding his own ground, and Li Keyong eyeing Luzhou. Wang Hui concluded the court could not enforce its will and firmly declined in favor of Changtu.
units.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was in the west; the Yellow and Pass regions were in turmoil; Fangli held territory on his own authority, while Li Keyong watched Luzhou. Hui judged that the court could not control matters and firmly yielded to Changtu.

units.zh: 昌圖治不三月輒去。
units.en: Changtu governed less than three months before departing.
units.literal: Changtu governed less than three months and then left.

units.zh: 方立更表李殷銳為刺史，謂潞險而人悍，數賊大帥為亂，欲銷懦之，乃徙治龍岡州，豪傑重遷，有懟言。
units.en: Fangli then recommended Li Yinrui as prefect, arguing that Luzhou was rugged and its people fierce, that successive governors had rebelled, and that he would break their spirit by moving the seat to Longgangzhou; local magnates resented the move and murmured in protest.
units.literal: Fangli further memorialized Li Yinrui as prefect, saying Lu was perilous and its people fierce, that great commanders had repeatedly rebelled, and wishing to break their spirit he moved the seat to Longgang Prefecture; the powerful gentry resented the relocation and there was angry talk.

units.zh: 會克用為河東節度使，昭義監軍祁審誨乞師求復昭義軍；
units.en: When Keyong became Hedong military governor, Zhaoyi army supervisor Qi Shenhui appealed for troops to restore the Zhaoyi command;
units.literal: It happened that Keyong became military governor of Hedong; the Zhaoyi army supervisor Qi Shenhui begged troops to restore the Zhaoyi army;

units.zh: 克用遣賀公雅、李筠、安金俊三部將擊潞州，為方立所破。
units.en: Keyong sent He Gongya, Li Jun, and An Jinjun against Luzhou, but Fangli defeated them.
units.literal: Keyong sent the three generals He Gongya, Li Jun, and An Jinjun to strike Luzhou, and they were defeated by Fangli.

units.zh: 又使李克修攻敗之，殺殷銳，遂並潞州，表克修為節度留後。
units.en: He then sent Li Kexiu, who defeated Fangli's forces, killed Yinrui, seized Luzhou, and recommended Kexiu as acting governor.
units.literal: He again sent Li Kexiu to attack and defeat them, killed Yinrui, thereupon annexed Luzhou, and memorialized Kexiu as acting military governor.

units.zh: 初，昭義有潞、邢、洺、磁四州。
units.en: Originally the Zhaoyi circuit comprised Luzhou, Xingzhou, Mingzhou, and Cizhou.
units.literal: Earlier Zhaoyi had the four prefectures of Lu, Xing, Ming, and Ci.

units.zh: 至是，方立自以山東三州為昭義，朝廷亦命克修，以潞州舊軍畀之，昭義有兩節自此始。
units.en: Fangli now held the three eastern prefectures as his own Zhaoyi command while the court appointed Kexiu over Luzhou with its former garrison—thus the circuit was split in two.
units.literal: At this point Fangli on his own took the three eastern prefectures as Zhaoyi; the court also appointed Kexiu and gave him the old Lu army, and from this time there were two Zhaoyi commands.

units.zh: 克修，字崇遠，克用從父弟。
units.en: Kexiu, courtesy name Chongyuan, was Li Keyong's paternal cousin.
units.literal: Kexiu, style name Chongyuan, was Keyong's younger cousin on the father's side.

units.zh: 精馳射，常從征伐，自左營軍使擢留後，進檢校司空。
units.en: An expert horseman and archer, he campaigned constantly, rose from commander of the Left Camp to acting governor, and was promoted to acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: Skilled at mounted archery, he often followed campaigns; from Left Camp army commander he was promoted to acting governor and advanced to acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 方立倚朱全忠為助，故無用擊邢、洺、磁無虛歲，地為鬥場，人不能稼。
units.en: Fangli leaned on Zhu Quanzhong for support, yet Xing, Ming, and Ci were attacked every year without respite until the region was nothing but a battlefield and farming ceased.
units.literal: Fangli relied on Zhu Quanzhong for aid, so year after year there were attacks on Xing, Ming, and Ci without pause; the land became a battleground and people could not farm.

units.zh: 光啟二年，克修擊邢州，取故鎮，進攻武安，方立將呂臻、馬爽戰焦岡，為克修所破，斬首萬級，執臻等，拔武安、臨洺、邯鄲、沙河。
units.en: In 886 Kexiu attacked Xingzhou, recovered the old seat, and pressed on Wu'an; Fangli's generals Lü Zhen and Ma Shuang met him at Jiaogang and were routed—ten thousand heads were taken, Zhen captured, and Wu'an, Linming, Handan, and Shahe fell.
units.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Kexiu attacked Xing Prefecture, took the old seat, and advanced on Wu'an; Fangli's generals Lü Zhen and Ma Shuang fought at Jiaogang, were defeated by Kexiu, ten thousand heads were cut off, Zhen and the others were seized, and Wu'an, Linming, Handan, and Shahe were taken.

units.zh: 克用以安金俊為邢州刺史招撫之。
units.en: Keyong appointed An Jinjun prefect of Xingzhou to pacify the region.
units.literal: Keyong used An Jinjun as prefect of Xing to win them over and pacify them.

units.zh: 方立丐兵於王鎔，鎔以兵三萬赴之，克修還。
units.en: Fangli appealed to Wang Rong for troops; Rong sent thirty thousand men, and Kexiu withdrew.
units.literal: Fangli begged troops from Wang Rong; Rong sent thirty thousand men to his aid, and Kexiu withdrew.

units.zh: 後二年，方立督部將奚忠信兵三萬攻遼州，以金啖赫連鐸與連和。
units.en: Two years later Fangli led his general Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand men against Liaozhou, bribing Helian Duo to join the campaign.
units.literal: Two years later Fangli supervised his subordinate general Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops to attack Lia Prefecture, using gold to win Helian Duo to join in alliance.

units.zh: 會契丹攻鐸師失期，忠信三分其兵，鼓而行，克用伏兵於險，忠信前軍沒，既戰，大敗，執忠信，餘眾走脫，歸者才十二。
units.en: When Khitan raids delayed Duo's army, Zhongxin split his force in three columns and marched with drums beating; Keyong ambushed him in a pass, destroyed his vanguard, and routed the main body; Zhongxin was captured, and only twelve men made it back.
units.literal: It happened that the Khitan attack on Duo made his army miss the rendezvous; Zhongxin divided his force in three and advanced with drums; Keyong set ambush in a defile; Zhongxin's vanguard was destroyed, and once battle was joined he was utterly defeated; Zhongxin was seized, the rest fled, and only twelve returned.

units.zh: 龍紀元年，克用使李罕之、李存孝擊邢，攻磁、洺，方立戰琉璃陂，大敗，禽其二將，被斧鑕，徇邢壘，呼曰：「孟公速降，有能斬其首者，假三州節度使。」
units.en: In 889 Keyong sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao against Xingzhou and into Ci and Ming; Fangli met them at Liuli Dam, was crushed, and lost both generals; the captives were shackled and displayed before the walls of Xing with the cry, "Lord Meng, surrender at once! Whoever brings me his head shall govern the three prefectures."
units.literal: In the first year of Longji, Keyong sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao to strike Xing and attack Ci and Ming; Fangli fought at Liuli Dam, was utterly defeated, and the two generals were captured; they were put in cangues and paraded before the Xing ramparts, crying: "Lord Meng, surrender quickly! Whoever can cut off his head shall be given acting governor of the three prefectures."

units.zh: 方立力屈，又屬州殘墮，人心恐，性剛急，待下少恩，夜自行陴，兵皆倨告勞，自顧不可復振，乃還，引鴆自殺。
units.en: His strength was spent, his prefectures in ruins, and morale shattered; harsh by nature and sparing of kindness, he toured the walls at night while the troops answered with insolent complaints of exhaustion. Convinced he could not recover, he went back inside, drank poison, and died.
units.literal: Fangli's strength was spent; moreover the prefectures were ruined and crumbling, hearts were fearful; his nature was stern and impatient, his kindness to subordinates slight; he walked the parapets at night, and the soldiers were all insolent in reporting fatigue; seeing he could not recover, he returned, took poison, and killed himself.

units.zh: 從弟遷，素得士心，眾推為節度留後，請援於全忠。
units.en: His cousin Qian, beloved by the troops, was acclaimed acting governor and appealed to Quanzhong for aid.
units.literal: His cousin Qian, who had long won the soldiers' hearts, was pushed by the masses as acting military governor and asked aid of Quanzhong.

units.zh: 全忠方攻時溥，不即至，命王虔裕以精甲數百赴之，假道羅宏信，不許，乃趨間入邢州。
units.en: Quanzhong was besieging Shi Pu and could not come immediately; he sent Wang Yuyu with several hundred elite troops by a secret path after Luo Hongxin refused passage, and they slipped into Xingzhou.
units.literal: Quanzhong was just attacking Shi Pu and did not arrive at once; he ordered Wang Yuyu with several hundred picked armored men to go to his aid; he asked passage through Luo Hongxin, who refused, and so hurried by a hidden route into Xing.

units.zh: 大順元年，存孝復攻邢，遷挈邢、洺、磁三州降，執王虔裕三百人獻之；
units.en: In 890 Cunxiao attacked Xingzhou again; Qian surrendered the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and Ci and handed over Wang Yuyu and three hundred of his men;
units.literal: In the first year of Dashun, Cunxiao again attacked Xing; Qian brought the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and Ci to surrender, seized three hundred men including Wang Yuyu and presented them;

units.zh: 遂遷太原，表安金俊為邢、洺、磁團練使，以遷為汾州刺史。
units.en: Qian was then transferred to Taiyuan while An Jinjun was appointed training commissioner over the three prefectures and Qian named prefect of Fenzhou.
units.literal: thereupon he was moved to Taiyuan; An Jinjun was memorialized as training commissioner of Xing, Ming, and Ci, and Qian was made prefect of Fen.

units.zh: 《歐陽史》云：天復元年，梁遣氏叔琮攻晉，出天井關，遷開門降，為梁兵鄉道以攻太原，不克；
units.en: Ouyang Xiu's history records that in 901 the Liang sent Shi Shuzong against Jin through Tianjing Pass; Qian opened the gates, guided the Liang army toward Taiyuan, and failed to take the city;
units.literal: Ouyang Xiu's history states: In the first year of Tianfu the Liang sent Shi Shuzong to attack Jin, coming out through Tianjing Pass; Qian opened the gates and surrendered, guiding the Liang army to attack Taiyuan, but they did not take it;

units.zh: 叔琮軍還過潞，以遷歸於梁。
units.en: on the return march Shuzong passed through Luzhou and delivered Qian to the Liang.
units.literal: Shuzong's army on returning passed through Lu and handed Qian over to the Liang.

units.zh: 梁太祖惡其反覆，殺之。）〉
units.en: The Liang founder despised his treachery and had him executed.)〉
units.literal: The Liang founder hated his fickleness and killed him.)〉

units.zh: 張文禮，燕人也。
units.en: Zhang Wenli was a native of Yan.
units.literal: Zhang Wenli was a man of Yan.

units.zh: 初為劉仁恭裨將，性凶險，多奸謀，辭氣庸下，與人交言，癖於不遜，自少及長，專蓄異謀。
units.en: He began as a staff officer under Liu Rengong, a man fierce and treacherous, coarse in speech and habitually insolent in conversation; from youth he had nursed one conspiracy after another.
units.literal: He first served as staff officer to Liu Rengong; his nature was fierce and perilous, full of treacherous schemes; his speech and manner were base; in conversing with others he was addicted to insolence; from youth to age he constantly harbored strange plots.

units.zh: 及從劉守文之滄州，委將偏師。
units.en: When he followed Liu Shouwen to Cangzhou, he was given command of a detached force.
units.literal: When he followed Liu Shouwen to Cang Prefecture, he was entrusted with a detached division.

units.zh: 守文省父燕薊，據城為亂。
units.en: Shouwen went up to Yan and Ji to visit his father, then seized the city and rebelled.
units.literal: Shouwen went to visit his father in Yan and Ji, seized the city, and rebelled.

units.zh: 及敗，奔於王鎔。
units.en: When the rebellion collapsed he fled to Wang Rong.
units.literal: When defeated he fled to Wang Rong.

units.zh: 察鎔不親政事，遂曲事當權者，以求衒達。
units.en: Seeing that Rong neglected government, he cultivated those in power to advance himself.
units.literal: Seeing that Rong did not attend to government himself, he thereupon curried favor with those in power to seek display and advancement.

units.zh: 每對鎔自言有將才，孫、吳、韓、白，莫己若也。
units.en: He told Rong repeatedly that as a commander he stood with Sun Wu, Wu Qi, Han Xin, and Bai Qi—and that none surpassed him.
units.literal: Whenever he faced Rong he declared himself possessed of general's talent—none could compare with him to Sun Wu, Wu Qi, Han Xin, or Bai Qi.

units.zh: 鎔賞其言，給遺甚厚，因錄為義男，賜姓，名德明，由是每令將兵。
units.en: Rong was impressed, lavished gifts on him, adopted him as a son, granted him the surname and the name Deming, and thereafter regularly put him in command.
units.literal: Rong prized his words and gave him very generous gifts; he was thereupon enrolled as an adopted son, granted the clan name, and named Deming; from this he was repeatedly ordered to lead troops.

units.zh: 自柏鄉戰勝之後，常從莊宗行營。
units.en: After the victory at Baixiang he often campaigned with Emperor Zhuangzong's headquarters.
units.literal: After the victory at Bai Township he often followed Emperor Zhuangzong's field headquarters.

units.zh: 素不知書，亦無方略，惟於懦兵之中萋菲上將，言甲不知進退，乙不識軍機，以此軍人推為良將。
units.en: Illiterate and devoid of strategy, he won favor among timid soldiers by slandering their commanders—one knew nothing of advance or retreat, another nothing of tactics—and on that basis the men hailed him as a fine general.
units.literal: He had never known books and had no strategy; only among cowardly soldiers did he slander superiors, saying that A did not know advance and retreat and B did not understand military affairs—by this the troops pushed him as a good general.

units.zh: 初，梁將楊師厚在魏州，文禮領趙兵三萬夜掠經、宗，因侵貝郡。
units.en: When the Liang general Yang Shihou held Weizhou, Wenli led thirty thousand Zhao troops on a night raid into Jing and Zong and pressed into Bei commandery.
units.literal: Earlier the Liang general Yang Shihou was at Wei Prefecture; Wenli led thirty thousand Zhao troops by night to plunder Jing and Zong and thereby invaded Bei commandery.

units.zh: 師厚先率步騎數千人，設伏於唐店。
units.en: Shihou marched ahead with several thousand foot and horse and laid an ambush at Tangdian.
units.literal: Shihou first led several thousand infantry and cavalry and set an ambush at Tang Inn.

units.zh: 文禮大掠而旋，士皆卷甲束兵，夜凱歌，行至唐店，師厚伏兵四面圍合，殺戮殆盡，文禮單騎僅免。
units.en: Wenli looted heavily and withdrew with his men singing victory songs in the night, armor bundled on their backs; at Tangdian Shihou's ambush closed on every side and slaughtered them almost to a man—Wenli alone escaped on horseback.
units.literal: Wenli plundered greatly and turned back; the soldiers all rolled up their armor and bound their weapons, singing victory songs at night; when they reached Tang Inn, Shihou's hidden troops closed in on all sides and slaughtered them nearly to the last man; Wenli alone on horseback barely escaped.

units.zh: 自爾猶對諸將大言，或讓之曰：「唐店之功，不須多伐。」
units.en: Even afterward he bragged before the other generals until one reproved him: "The affair at Tangdian is hardly something to boast about."
units.literal: From then on he still boasted greatly before the generals; someone reproached him, saying: "The achievement at Tang Inn needs no great boasting."

units.zh: 文禮大慚。
units.en: Wenli flushed with shame.
units.literal: Wenli was deeply ashamed.

units.zh: 在鎮州既久，見其政荒人僻，常蓄異圖；
units.en: After long service at Zhenzhou he saw negligent government and an isolated populace, and constantly nursed rebellious designs;
units.literal: Having been long at Zhen Prefecture, he saw that its government was negligent and its people remote, and constantly harbored strange designs;

units.zh: 酒酣之後，對左右每泄惡言，聞者莫不寒心。
units.en: when drunk he would vent vicious threats to his attendants, chilling everyone who heard him.
units.literal: after wine had gone deep he often let fall evil words to those beside him, and hearers were all chilled in heart.

units.zh: 惟王鎔略無猜間，漸為腹心，乃以符習代其行營，以文禮為防城使，自此專伺間隙。
units.en: Wang Rong alone remained unsuspecting and drew him into his inner circle; he replaced Wenli in the field army with Fu Xi and made Wenli commissioner of city defense, after which Wenli watched only for his chance.
units.literal: Only Wang Rong was slightly without suspicion; Wenli gradually became his intimate, and Rong then replaced him in the field camp with Fu Xi and made Wenli city-defense commissioner—from this time he devoted himself solely to watching for openings.

units.zh: 及鎔殺李宏規，委政於其子昭祚。
units.en: When Rong executed Li Honggui he handed power to his son Zhaozuo.
units.literal: When Rong killed Li Honggui he entrusted government to his son Zhaozuo.

units.zh: 昭祚性逼戾，未識人間情偽，素養名持重，坐作貴人，既事權在手，朝夕欲代其父，向來附勢之徒，無不族滅。
units.en: Zhaozuo was harsh and ignorant of human affairs, having long cultivated an air of lofty dignity; once power was his he plotted day and night to supplant his father and exterminated to the last man every courtier who had once curried favor.
units.literal: Zhaozuo's nature was harsh and overbearing; he did not know the truth and falsity of human affairs; he had long cultivated reputation and gravity, sitting and acting as a noble; once power was in his hands he morning and evening wished to replace his father; those who had formerly clung to power were without exception exterminated to the clan.

units.zh: 初，李宏規、李藹持權用事，樹立親舊，分董要職，故奸宄之心不能搖動，文禮頗深畏憚。
units.en: Earlier Li Honggui and Li Ai had held real power, placing kin and allies in every key post, so that would-be traitors could not stir—and Wenli feared them deeply.
units.literal: Earlier Li Honggui and Li Ai held power and managed affairs, set up kin and old associates, and divided supervision of key posts, so the hearts of traitors could not be stirred; Wenli was quite deeply fearful and restrained.

units.zh: 及宏規見殺，其部下五百人懼罪，將欲奔竄，聚泣偶語，未有所之。
units.en: After Honggui's execution his five hundred followers, fearing punishment, gathered in tears and whispered among themselves, unsure where to flee.
units.literal: When Honggui was killed, his five hundred followers feared punishment and were about to flee; they gathered weeping and speaking in low voices, not yet knowing where to go.

units.zh: 文禮因其離心，密以奸辭激之曰：「令公命我盡坑爾曹，我念爾十餘年荷戈隨我，為家為國，我若不即殺爾，則得罪於令公；
units.en: Wenli exploited their disaffection and secretly incited them: "The lord has ordered me to bury you all alive. I remember how for more than ten years you bore arms and followed me, for family and state; if I do not kill you at once, I offend the lord;
units.literal: Wenli, because of their alienation of heart, secretly used treacherous words to incite them, saying: "The lord has ordered me to bury you all alive. I think of how for more than ten years you bore weapons and followed me for home and state; if I do not kill you at once I offend the lord;

units.zh: 我若不言，又負爾輩。」
units.en: if I keep silent, I fail you."
units.literal: if I do not speak, I again fail you all."

units.zh: 眾軍皆泣。
units.en: The soldiers wept.
units.literal: All the troops wept.

units.zh: 是夜作亂，殺王鎔父子，舉族灰滅，惟留王昭祚妻朱氏通梁人；
units.en: That night they rose in mutiny, killed Wang Rong and his son, and annihilated the clan—only Zhaozuo's wife Lady Zhu, who had connections with the Liang, was spared;
units.literal: That night they mutinied, killed Wang Rong father and son, and wiped out the whole clan to ashes; only Wang Zhaozuo's wife the Lady Zhu, who had ties to Liang men, was spared;

units.zh: 尋間道告於梁曰：「王氏喪於亂軍，普寧公主無恙。」
units.en: she soon sent word by a secret path to the Liang: "The Wang house has fallen to mutineers, but Princess Puning is safe."
units.literal: soon by a hidden route she reported to the Liang: "The Wang house has perished among the mutinous troops; Princess Puning is unharmed."

units.zh: 文禮徇賊帥張友順所請，因為留後，於潭城視事。
units.en: Wenli acceded to the bandit leader Zhang Youshun's request, took the title of acting governor, and administered affairs from Tancheng.
units.literal: Wenli yielded to the request of the bandit chief Zhang Youshun and thereupon became acting governor, conducting affairs at Tancheng.

units.zh: 以事上聞，兼要節旄，尋亦奉箋勸進，莊宗姑示含容，乃可其請。
units.en: He reported to the throne and demanded the commissioner's insignia; he soon sent a memorial urging Zhuangzong's accession, and Zhuangzong, for the moment forbearing, granted his request.
units.literal: He reported the matter upward and also demanded the commander's banner; soon he also submitted a memorial urging advancement; Emperor Zhuangzong for the moment showed forbearance and approved his request.

units.zh: 文禮比廝役小人，驟居人上，行步動息，皆不自安。
units.en: A menial who had risen overnight, Wenli could not compose himself in gait or breath.
units.literal: Wenli compared to a menial servant and petty man, suddenly placed above others—his walking, moving, and breathing were all without ease.

units.zh: 出則千餘人露刃相隨，日殺不辜，道路以目，常慮我師問罪，奸心百端。
units.en: Whenever he went abroad more than a thousand men with drawn swords followed; he killed innocents daily until travelers dared only glance sideways; he constantly feared imperial retribution and spun endless plots.
units.literal: When he went out more than a thousand men with bared blades followed; daily he killed the innocent; people in the road looked with eyes alone; he constantly feared our army would call him to account, and his treacherous heart had a hundred schemes.

units.zh: 南通朱氏，北結契丹，往往擒獲其使，莊宗遣人送還，文禮由是愈恐。
units.en: He courted the Zhu clan in the south and the Khitan in the north, often seizing their envoys until Zhuangzong returned them—which only deepened Wenli's terror.
units.literal: South he connected with the Zhu clan, north he joined the Khitan; he often seized their envoys; Zhuangzong sent men to return them, and Wenli from this grew ever more fearful.

units.zh: 是歲八月，莊宗遣閻寶、史建瑭及趙將符習等率王鎔本軍進討。
units.en: In the eighth month Zhuangzong sent Yan Bao, Shi Jiantan, and the Zhao general Fu Xi with Wang Rong's former army to suppress him.
units.literal: In the eighth month of that year Zhuangzong sent Yan Bao, Shi Jiantan, and the Zhao general Fu Xi and others to lead Wang Rong's original army forward to punish him.

units.zh: 師興，文禮病疽腹，及聞史建瑭攻下趙州，驚悸而卒。
units.en: As the campaign opened Wenli lay ill with an abdominal abscess; when he heard that Shi Jiantan had taken Zhaozhou he died of shock.
units.literal: When the army rose, Wenli was ill with carbuncle in the belly; when he heard that Shi Jiantan had taken Zhao Prefecture he died of shock and palpitation.

units.zh: 其子處瑾、處球秘不發喪，軍府內外，皆不知之，每日於寢宮問安。
units.en: His sons Chujin and Chuqiu concealed the death; inside and outside headquarters none knew, and each day they sent greetings to the bedchamber as if their father still lived.
units.literal: His sons Chujin and Chuqiu concealed the death and did not announce the mourning; inside and outside the military headquarters none knew; daily at the sleeping palace they inquired after his health.

units.zh: 處瑾與其腹心韓正時參決大事，同謀奸惡。
units.en: Chujin and his confidant Han Zhengshi decided major affairs together and plotted further treachery.
units.literal: Chujin with his intimate Han Zhengshi jointly decided great affairs and conspired in treacherous evil.

units.zh: 初，文禮疽未發時，舉家咸見鬼物，昏瞑之後或歌或哭，又野河色變如血，遊魚多死，浮於水上，識者知其必敗。
units.en: Before Wenli's abscess broke, his household saw apparitions; after dark there were songs and wails; the wild river turned the color of blood and fish died in shoals upon the surface—those who read omens knew he was doomed.
units.literal: Earlier, before Wenli's carbuncle broke out, the whole household all saw ghostly things; after dusk there was singing or weeping; moreover the wild river changed color like blood, wandering fish mostly died and floated on the water—those who knew saw he must fail.

units.zh: 十九年三月，閻寶為處瑾所敗，莊宗以李嗣昭代之。
units.en: In the third month of the nineteenth year Yan Bao was defeated by Chujin, and Zhuangzong replaced him with Li Sizhao.
units.literal: In the third month of the nineteenth year Yan Bao was defeated by Chujin; Zhuangzong replaced him with Li Sizhao.

units.zh: 四月，嗣昭為流矢所中，尋卒於師，命李存進繼之。
units.en: In the fourth month Sizhao was struck by a stray arrow and died in camp; Li Cunjin was ordered to take his place.
units.literal: In the fourth month Sizhao was struck by a stray arrow and soon died in the army; Li Cunjin was ordered to succeed him.

units.zh: 存進亦以戰歿，乃以符存審為北面招討使，攻鎮州。
units.en: Cunjin too fell in battle, and Fu Cunshen was appointed northern campaign commissioner to besiege Zhenzhou.
units.literal: Cunjin also died in battle; thereupon Fu Cunshen was made northern campaign commissioner to attack Zhen Prefecture.

units.zh: 是時，處瑾危蹙日甚。
units.en: Chujin's situation grew more desperate by the day.
units.literal: At this time Chujin's peril pressed daily more severe.

units.zh: 昭義軍節度判官任圜馳至城下，諭以禍福，處瑾登陴以誠告，乃遣牙將張彭送款於行台。
units.en: Ren Yuan, administrative aide of the Zhaoyi circuit, rode to the walls and explained the consequences; Chujin mounted the battlements in apparent sincerity and sent his officer Zhang Peng to offer surrender to headquarters.
units.literal: The Zhaoyi circuit administrative aide Ren Yuan galloped to below the walls and instructed him in fortune and disaster; Chujin mounted the parapet and with sincerity declared himself; he then sent the gate officer Zhang Peng to offer surrender to the field headquarters.

units.zh: 俄而符存審師至城下。
units.en: Soon afterward Fu Cunshen's army reached the walls.
units.literal: Shortly Fu Cunshen's army arrived below the walls.

units.zh: 是夜，趙將李再豐之子衝投縋以接王師，故諸軍登城，遲明畢入，獲處瑾、處球、處琪，並其母及同惡人等，皆折足送行台，鎮人請醢而食之。
units.en: That night Li Zaifeng's son Chong lowered a rope to admit the imperial army; the troops scaled the walls and by dawn had taken the city. Chujin, Chuqiu, Chuqi, their mother, and their accomplices were captured, their legs broken, and sent to headquarters; the townspeople begged that they be minced for food.
units.literal: That night the Zhao general Li Zaifeng's son Chong cast a rope down to receive the royal army; therefore the various forces ascended the walls; at delayed dawn they had all entered, seized Chujin, Chuqiu, and Chuqi, together with their mother and fellow evildoers; all had their feet broken and were sent to headquarters; the people of Zhen requested they be minced and eaten.

units.zh: 又發文禮之屍，磔之於市。
units.en: Wenli's corpse was exhumed and dismembered in the marketplace.
units.literal: They also disinterred Wenli's corpse and exposed it on the market.

units.zh: 董璋，本梁之驍將也。
units.en: Dong Zhang had been one of the Liang's fiercest generals.
units.literal: Dong Zhang was originally a fierce general of the Liang.

units.zh: 幼與高季興、孔循俱事豪士李七郎為童仆。
units.en: As a boy he served the swaggering Master Li the Seventh alongside Gao Jixing and Kong Xun as a household page.
units.literal: In youth he with Gao Jixing and Kong Xun all served the bold man Master Li the Seventh as child servants.

units.zh: 李初名讓，常以厚賄奉梁祖，梁祖寵之，因畜為假子，賜姓朱，名友讓。
units.en: Li, originally named Rang, lavished bribes on the Liang founder until the emperor favored him, adopted him as a son, granted the Zhu surname, and named him Yourang.
units.literal: Li's original name was Rang; he constantly offered rich bribes to the Liang founder, who favored him and thereupon raised him as an adopted son, granting the surname Zhu and the name Yourang.

units.zh: 璋既壯，得隸於梁祖帳下，後以軍功遷為列校。
units.en: When Zhang came of age he entered the Liang founder's service and rose through battlefield merit to company commander.
units.literal: When Zhang had grown strong he came under the Liang founder's banner, and later through military merit was promoted to company commander.

units.zh: 梁龍德末，潞州李繼韜送款於梁。
units.en: Near the end of the Longde reign Li Jitao of Luzhou surrendered to the Liang.
units.literal: At the end of Liang Longde, Luzhou's Li Jitao offered surrender to the Liang.

units.zh: 時潞將裴約方領兵戍澤州，不徇繼韜之命，據城以自固。
units.en: The Lu general Pei Yue was then garrisoning Zezhou, refused Jitao's orders, and held the city on his own account.
units.literal: At that time the Lu general Pei Yue was just leading troops garrisoning Ze Prefecture, did not follow Jitao's order, and held the city to firm himself.

units.zh: 梁末帝遣璋攻陷澤州，遂授澤州刺史。
units.en: The last Liang emperor sent Zhang to capture Zezhou and appointed him its prefect.
units.literal: The Liang final emperor sent Zhang to attack and take Ze Prefecture, and thereupon appointed him prefect of Ze.

units.zh: 是歲，莊宗入汴，璋來朝，莊宗素聞其名，優以待之。
units.en: That year, when Zhuangzong entered Bian, Zhang came to court; Zhuangzong had long known his reputation and received him generously.
units.literal: That year Zhuangzong entered Bian; Zhang came to court; Zhuangzong had long heard his name and treated him with favor.

units.zh: 尋令卻赴舊任，歲餘代歸。
units.en: He was soon sent back to his former post and returned to court a year later when relieved.
units.literal: Soon he was ordered to return to his old post; after more than a year he was replaced and came back.

units.zh: 時郭崇韜當國，待璋尤厚。
units.en: Guo Chongtao then dominated the government and treated Zhang with exceptional favor.
units.literal: At that time Guo Chongtao held power and treated Zhang especially generously.

units.zh: 同光三年夏，命為邠州留後，三年秋，正授旄鉞。
units.en: In the summer of Tongguang 3 he was named acting governor of Binzhou; that autumn he received the full commissioner's insignia.
units.literal: In summer of Tongguang year three he was ordered acting governor of Bin Prefecture; in autumn of year three he was formally given the banner and axe.

units.zh: 九月，大舉伐蜀，以璋為行營右廂馬步都虞候。
units.en: In the ninth month a major expedition against Shu was launched, with Zhang as superintendent of the right wing of the field army.
units.literal: In the ninth month a great campaign was launched against Shu; Zhang was made right-wing horse-and-foot superintendent of the field camp.

units.zh: 時郭崇韜為招討使，凡有軍機，皆召璋參決。
units.en: Guo Chongtao commanded the expedition and summoned Zhang to every council on military affairs.
units.literal: At that time Guo Chongtao was campaign commissioner; whenever there was military planning Zhang was summoned to join in the decision.

units.zh: 是冬，蜀平，以璋為劍南東川節度副大使，知節度事。
units.en: Shu fell that winter, and Zhang was made deputy military governor of Eastern Chuan with full control of circuit affairs.
units.literal: That winter Shu was pacified; Zhang was made deputy military governor of Eastern Chuan of Jiannan and managed circuit affairs.

units.zh: 天成初，加檢校太傅。
units.en: At the opening of the Tiancheng reign he was promoted to acting Grand Tutor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was added acting Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 二年，加同平章事。
units.en: In the second year he was made a Fellow of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the second year he was added Fellow of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 是時安重誨當國，采人邪謀，言孟知祥必不為國家使，惟董璋性忠義，可特寵任，令圖知祥。
units.en: An Chonghui then held power and listened to slanderers who said Meng Zhixiang would never serve the throne, whereas Dong Zhang was loyal and should be specially favored to counter Zhixiang.
units.literal: At that time An Chonghui held power, accepted men's treacherous counsel, saying Meng Zhixiang would certainly not serve the state, only Dong Zhang by nature was loyal and righteous and could be specially favored and entrusted to plot against Zhixiang.

units.zh: 又璋之子光業為宮苑使，在朝結托勢援，爭言璋之善，知祥之惡。
units.en: Zhang's son Guangye, palace park commissioner, cultivated powerful allies at court and ceaselessly praised his father while denouncing Zhixiang.
units.literal: Also Zhang's son Guangye was palace park commissioner; in court he formed ties with powerful backers, competing to speak of Zhang's goodness and Zhixiang's evil.

units.zh: 恩寵既優，故璋益恣其暴戾。
units.en: With imperial favor secure, Zhang grew ever more violent and overbearing.
units.literal: Favor and grace being already generous, Zhang therefore grew ever more unrestrained in violence.

units.zh: 初，奉使東川者，皆言璋不恭於朝廷。
units.en: Envoys returning from Eastern Chuan had long reported Zhang's disrespect toward the court.
units.literal: Earlier envoys to Eastern Chuan all said Zhang was disrespectful to the court.

units.zh: 四年夏，時明宗將議郊天，遣客省使李仁矩齎詔示諭兩川，又遣安重誨馳書於璋，以征貢奉，約以五十萬為數。
units.en: In the summer of the fourth year, as Mingzong prepared for the suburban sacrifice, he sent palace envoy Li Renju with an edict to the two Chuan and dispatched An Chonghui with a letter demanding five hundred thousand in tribute from Zhang.
units.literal: In summer of the fourth year, when Mingzong was about to discuss suburban sacrifice, he sent palace envoy Li Renju with an edict to instruct the two Chuan, and also sent An Chonghui with a rushed letter to Zhang demanding tribute payment, set at five hundred thousand as the figure.

units.zh: 既而璋訴以地狹民貧，許貢十萬而已。
units.en: Zhang protested that his territory was poor and narrow, and tribute was reduced to one hundred thousand.
units.literal: Thereafter Zhang pleaded that the land was narrow and the people poor, and only one hundred thousand tribute was permitted.

units.zh: 翌日，璋於衙署設宴以召仁矩，日既中而不至，璋使人偵之，仁矩方擁倡婦與賓友酣飲於驛亭。
units.en: The next day Zhang gave a banquet at headquarters for Renju, but noon passed and he did not appear; spies found Renju in the relay station drinking with singing girls and guests.
units.literal: The next day Zhang set a banquet at the government office to summon Renju; the sun had already passed noon and he had not come; Zhang sent men to spy on him—Renju was just embracing singing girls and drinking deeply with guests at the relay pavilion.

units.zh: 璋大怒，遽領數百人，執持戈戟，驟入驛中，令洞開其門。
units.en: Zhang flew into a rage, led several hundred armed men into the relay station, and ordered the doors broken open.
units.literal: Zhang was greatly enraged, immediately led several hundred men holding spears and halberds, rushed into the relay station, and ordered the doors forced wide open.

units.zh: 仁矩惶駭，走入閣中，良久引出。
units.en: Renju fled in terror to an inner room and was dragged out only after a long delay.
units.literal: Renju was terrified, ran into a side room, and after a long while was brought out.

units.zh: 璋坐，立仁矩於階下，戟手罵曰：「當我作魏博都監，爾為通引小將，其時去就，已有等威。
units.en: Zhang seated himself and made Renju stand below the steps, then pointed at him and raged: "When I was inspector of Weibo you were a mere escort officer—even then there was rank between us.
units.literal: Zhang sat; Renju was made to stand below the steps; Zhang pointed with folded hands and cursed: "When I was inspector general of Weibo, you were a mere guide-and-escort petty officer; even then in coming and going there was already rank and awe between us.

units.zh: 今日我為藩侯，爾銜君命，宿張筵席，比為使臣，保敢至午不來，自共風塵耽酗，豈於王事如此不恭！
units.en: Today I am a feudal lord and you bear the emperor's commission, yet you carouse in a relay station and dare not appear by noon for my feast—how can an envoy treat the throne's business with such contempt!
units.literal: Today I am a feudal lord and you bear the Son of Heaven's command, yet you spread a banquet in a guest lodge and as an envoy dare not come by noon, yourself indulging in drinking in the dust of the road—how toward royal affairs can you be so disrespectful!

units.zh: 隻如西川解斬客省使李嚴，謂我不能斬公耶！」
units.en: Western Chuan executed the envoy Li Yan—do you think I cannot do the same to you!"
units.literal: Just as Western Chuan once executed the palace envoy Li Yan—do you think I cannot execute you!"

units.zh: 因目肘腋，欲令執拽仁矩，仁矩涕淚拜告，僅而獲免。
units.en: He signaled his attendants to seize Renju, who wept and kowtowed until he barely escaped with his life.
units.literal: He then signaled with his eyes to those at his elbows, wishing to have them seize and drag Renju; Renju wept and kowtowed begging, barely escaping with his life.

units.zh: 璋乃馳騎入衙，竟徹饌而不召。
units.en: Zhang rode back to headquarters and dismissed the feast without ever summoning Renju.
units.literal: Zhang then galloped into the government office and finally cleared the feast without summoning him.

units.zh: 洎仁矩復命，益言璋不法。
units.en: On his return Renju reported Zhang's misconduct at even greater length.
units.literal: When Renju returned to report he spoke all the more of Zhang's lawlessness.

units.zh: 未幾，重誨奏以仁矩為閬州團練使，尋升為節鎮。
units.en: Soon afterward Chonghui recommended Renju as training commissioner of Langzhou, then promoted him to full military governor.
units.literal: Before long Chonghui memorialized making Renju training commissioner of Lang Prefecture, soon promoted to full command.

units.zh: 長興元年夏，明宗以郊禋禮畢，加璋檢校太尉。
units.en: In the summer of the first Changxing year, after Mingzong completed the suburban sacrifice, Zhang was promoted to acting Grand Marshal.
units.literal: In summer of the first year of Changxing, after Mingzong's suburban sacrifice was complete, Zhang was added acting Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 時兩川刺史嘗以兵為牙軍，小郡不下五百人，璋已疑間，及聞除仁矩鎮閬州，璋由是謀反乃決。
units.en: The two Chuan governors each maintained guard armies of at least five hundred men even in small prefectures; Zhang already suspected encirclement, and when he learned Renju had been appointed to Langzhou his decision to rebel was fixed.
units.literal: At that time the two Chuan prefects often used troops as guard armies, small prefectures not less than five hundred men; Zhang already had suspicions of separation; when he heard of Renju's appointment to Lang Prefecture, Zhang's rebellion was thereby decided.

units.zh: 仍先與其子光業書曰：「朝廷割吾支郡為節制，屯兵三千，是殺我必矣。
units.en: He wrote first to his son Guangye: "The court has carved out my subordinate prefectures as a separate command and posted three thousand troops—that is a death sentence.
units.literal: He first wrote his son Guangye: "The court has carved away my subordinate prefectures to make a command and stationed three thousand troops—that is to kill me for certain.

units.zh: 爾見樞要道吾言，如朝廷更發一騎入斜穀，則吾必反，與汝決矣！」
units.en: Tell the grand councilors for me: if the court sends even one more rider through Xiegu Pass, I will rebel and break with you forever!"
units.literal: You see the grand councilors and speak my words: if the court sends even one more rider into Xiegu, I will certainly rebel and part with you!"

units.zh: 光業以書呈樞密承旨李虔徽。
units.en: Guangye presented the letter to Secretariat drafter Li Qianhui.
units.literal: Guangye presented the letter to Secretariat drafter Li Qianhui.

units.zh: 會朝廷再發中使荀鹹乂將兵赴閬州，光業謂虔徽曰：「鹹乂未至，吾父必反。
units.en: When the court again sent the inner envoy Gou Xianyi with troops to Langzhou, Guangye told Qianhui: "Before Xianyi arrives my father will rebel.
units.literal: When the court again sent inner envoy Gou Xianyi with troops to Lang Prefecture, Guangye told Qianhui: "Before Xianyi arrives my father will rebel.

units.zh: 吾身不足惜，慮勞朝廷征發。
units.en: I do not value my own life, but I fear burdening the court with a campaign.
units.literal: My body is not worth sparing; I fear troubling the court with a campaign.

units.zh: 請停鹹乂之行，吾父必保常日。」
units.en: Stop Xianyi's march and my father will remain loyal."
units.literal: Please halt Xianyi's march and my father will surely keep to ordinary days."

units.zh: 重誨不從，鹹乂未至，璋已擅追綿州刺史武虔裕，囚於衙署。
units.en: Chonghui refused; before Xianyi arrived Zhang had already recalled Mianzhou prefect Wu Qianyu and imprisoned him at headquarters.
units.literal: Chonghui did not listen; before Xianyi arrived Zhang had already on his own authority recalled Mian prefect Wu Qianyu and imprisoned him in the government office.

units.zh: 虔裕，安重誨之心腹也，故先囚之。
units.en: Qianyu was Chonghui's trusted agent, and was seized first for that reason.
units.literal: Qianyu was Chonghui's trusted intimate, so he was imprisoned first.

units.zh: 五月，璋傳檄於利、閬、遂等州，責以間諜朝廷。
units.en: In the fifth month Zhang issued proclamations to Li, Lang, Sui, and neighboring prefectures accusing them of spying for the court.
units.literal: In the fifth month Zhang issued a proclamation to Li, Lang, Sui and other prefectures, accusing them of spying for the court.

units.zh: 尋率其兵陷閬州，擒節度使李仁矩、軍校姚洪等害之。
units.en: He soon marched on Langzhou, captured Governor Li Renju and the officer Yao Hong, and executed them.
units.literal: Soon he led his troops to take Lang Prefecture, seized military governor Li Renju and army officer Yao Hong and the others and killed them.

units.zh: 先是，璋欲謀叛，先遣使持厚幣於孟知祥，求為婚家。
units.en: Before his rebellion Zhang had sent envoys with rich gifts to Meng Zhixiang proposing a marriage alliance.
units.literal: Earlier when Zhang wished to rebel he first sent envoys with rich gifts to Meng Zhixiang seeking to become marriage kin.

units.zh: 且言為朝廷猜忌，將有替移，去則喪家，住亦致討，地狹兵少，獨力不任，願以小兒結婚愛女。
units.en: He said the court suspected him and would replace him; flight meant ruin, staying meant punishment; his territory was small and his army weak—he could not stand alone—and he asked to marry his son to Zhixiang's daughter.
units.literal: And he said he was suspected by the court and would be replaced; if he left he would lose his house, if he stayed he would also be punished; the land was narrow and troops few—alone he could not bear it—he wished to marry his young son to Zhixiang's beloved daughter.

units.zh: 時知祥亦貳於朝廷，因許以為援。
units.en: Zhixiang too was estranged from the court and promised him support.
units.literal: At that time Zhixiang also was disaffected from the court and therefore promised him as ally.

units.zh: 既而知祥出師以圍遂州，故璋攻閬州得恣其毒焉。
units.en: When Zhixiang later marched to besiege Suizhou, Zhang was free to ravage Langzhou at will.
units.literal: Later when Zhixiang marched out to besiege Sui Prefecture, Zhang could therefore attack Lang Prefecture at will in his cruelty.

units.zh: 其年秋，詔削奪璋在身官爵，命天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為東川行營招討使，率師以討之。
units.en: That autumn an edict stripped Zhang of his ranks and appointed Tianxiong governor Shi Jingtang Eastern Chuan campaign commissioner to lead troops against him.
units.literal: That autumn an edict stripped Zhang of all ranks he held; Tianxiong military governor Shi Jingtang was ordered as Eastern Chuan campaign commissioner to lead troops to punish him.

units.zh: 璋之子宮苑使光業並其族，並斬於洛陽。
units.en: Zhang's son Guangye, palace park commissioner, and his entire clan were executed at Luoyang.
units.literal: Zhang's son palace park commissioner Guangye and his entire clan were all executed at Luoyang.

units.zh: 及石敬瑭率師進討，以糧運不接，班師。
units.en: When Shi Jingtang marched against him, supply lines failed and the army withdrew.
units.literal: When Shi Jingtang led the army forward to punish him, because grain transport could not connect he withdrew the army.

units.zh: 明宗方務懷柔，乃放西川進奏官蘇願、東川軍將劉澄各歸本道，別無詔旨，隻云「兩務求安」。
units.en: Mingzong pursued conciliation, released Western Chuan memorial officer Su Yuan and Eastern Chuan officer Liu Cheng to their circuits, and issued no further orders beyond the phrase "both sides seek peace."
units.literal: Mingzong was then pursuing gentle appeasement, and released Western Chuan memorial officer Su Yuan and Eastern Chuan army officer Liu Cheng each to return to their circuits, with no other edict, only saying "both sides seek peace."

units.zh: 時孟知祥其骨肉在京師者俱無恙焉，因遣使報璋，欲連表稱謝。
units.en: Zhixiang's kin in the capital had been spared; he sent word to Zhang proposing a joint memorial of thanks to the throne.
units.literal: At that time Meng Zhixiang's kin in the capital were all unharmed; he thereupon sent an envoy to report to Zhang, wishing jointly to submit a memorial of thanks.

units.zh: 璋怒曰：「西川存得弟侄，遂欲再通朝廷，璋之兒孫已入黃泉，何謝之有！」
units.en: Zhang raged: "Western Chuan still has brothers and nephews alive, so you wish to reopen ties with the court—my sons and grandsons are already in the grave; what thanks is there to offer!"
units.literal: Zhang angrily said: "Western Chuan preserved brother and nephew, so they wish to reconnect with the court—Zhang's sons and grandsons have already entered the yellow springs; what thanks is there!"

units.zh: 自是璋疑知祥背己，始構隙矣。
units.en: From that moment Zhang suspected Zhixiang had betrayed him, and the rift between them began.
units.literal: From this Zhang suspected Zhixiang had turned against him and first formed a breach.

units.zh: 三年四月，璋率所部兵萬餘人以襲知祥。
units.en: In the fourth month of the third year Zhang led more than ten thousand men in a surprise attack on Zhixiang.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the third year Zhang led more than ten thousand of his troops to strike Zhixiang.

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·趙季良傳》：季良嘗與知祥從容語曰：「璋性狼戾，若堅守一城，攻之難克。」
units.en: (From the biography of Zhao Jiliang in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: Jiliang once told Zhixiang in private, "Zhang is brutal and savage; if he holds a single city firm, he will be hard to defeat."
units.literal: (From the Biography of Zhao Jiliang in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: Jiliang once spoke at ease with Zhixiang, saying: "Zhang's nature is wolfish and violent; if he firmly holds one city, attacking him is hard to overcome."

units.zh: 及聞璋起兵，知祥憂形於色。
units.en: When news came that Zhang had taken the field, worry showed on Zhixiang's face.
units.literal: When he heard Zhang had raised troops, Zhixiang's worry showed on his face.

units.zh: 季良曰：「璋不守巢穴，此天以授公也。」
units.en: Jiliang said, "Zhang has left his base undefended—Heaven is handing victory to you."
units.literal: Jiliang said: "Zhang does not guard his nest—Heaven thereby gives this to you, my lord."

units.zh: 既而璋果敗。）〉
units.en: Zhang was indeed defeated soon after.)〉
units.literal: Before long Zhang indeed was defeated.)〉

units.zh: 知祥與諸將率師拒之，戰於漢州之彌牟鎮。
units.en: Zhixiang and his generals marched to meet him and fought at Mizhen in Hanzhou.
units.literal: Zhixiang with the various generals led troops to resist, fighting at Mizhen in Han Prefecture.

units.zh: 璋軍大敗，得數十騎，復奔於東川。
units.en: Zhang's army was shattered; he escaped with only a few dozen horsemen back to Eastern Chuan.
units.literal: Zhang's army was utterly defeated; he had only several dozen horsemen and again fled to Eastern Chuan.

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·趙廷隱傳》：董璋襲廣漢，將攻成都，時東川廩藏充實，部下多敢死之士，其來也，眾皆畏之。
units.en: (From the biography of Zhao Tingyin in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: Dong Zhang raided Guanghan and was marching on Chengdu; Eastern Chuan's stores were full and his men were fearless; his advance struck terror into every heart.
units.literal: (From the Biography of Zhao Tingyin in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: Dong Zhang raided Guanghan and was about to attack Chengdu; at that time Eastern Chuan's granaries were full and his subordinates were mostly men who dared death; when they came, all were fearful.

units.zh: 知祥親督諸將，與璋戰雞縱橋前，頗為所挫。
units.en: Zhixiang personally led his generals against Zhang before Jizong Bridge and was driven back.
units.literal: Zhixiang personally supervised the generals and fought Zhang before Jizong Bridge, and was quite beaten back by him.

units.zh: 廷隱偽遁，璋逐之，知祥與張公鐸繼進，璋軍亂不成列，廷隱整陣，與知祥合擊之，璋軍大敗。）〉
units.en: Tingyin feigned retreat; Zhang pursued; Zhixiang and Zhang Gongduo pressed forward; Zhang's army fell into disorder; Tingyin reformed his line and joined Zhixiang in a combined assault that shattered Zhang's force.)〉
units.literal: Tingyin feigned flight; Zhang pursued him; Zhixiang with Zhang Gongduo followed in advance; Zhang's army was disordered and could not form ranks; Tingyin reformed the array and with Zhixiang jointly struck him; Zhang's army was utterly defeated.)〉

units.zh: 先是，前陵州刺史王暉為璋所邀，寓於東川，至是因璋之敗，率眾以害之，傳其首於西川。
units.en: Earlier the former Lingzhou prefect Wang Hui, whom Zhang had brought to Eastern Chuan, took advantage of Zhang's defeat, led troops to kill him, and sent his head to Western Chuan.
units.literal: Earlier former Ling prefect Wang Hui had been invited by Zhang and lodged in Eastern Chuan; on this occasion because of Zhang's defeat he led troops to kill him and sent his head to Western Chuan.

units.zh: 龍德末，閑居私第將期矣，晉主入汴，振謁見首罪，郭崇韜指振謂人曰：「人言李振乃一代奇才，吾今見之，乃常人耳！」
units.en: At the end of Longde he had lived in retirement nearly a year; when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen came to beg mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at him and said: "They call Li Zhen a wonder of the age—I see an ordinary man!"
units.literal: End of Longde, living in retirement at his private residence nearly a year, when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen paid court asking mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at Zhen and said to people: "People say Li Zhen is a generation's strange talent—I see him now and he is just an ordinary man!"

units.zh: 壬子，以內客省使、左衛大將軍李仁矩為閬州節度使。
units.en: On renzi Li Renju—inner guest commissioner and left guard senior general—became Lang commissioner.
units.literal: On renzi Inner Guest Bureau commissioner and Left Guard senior general Li Renju was made Lang military commissioner.

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent commanders Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji with troops to relieve Tongzhou; they fought below the walls.

units.zh: 夏四月己巳，晉王即唐帝位於魏州，改天祐二十年為同光元年。
units.en: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin took the Tang throne at Weizhou, renaming Tianyou 20 Tongguang 1.
units.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin assumed the Tang throne at Weizhou, changing Tianyou 20 to Tongguang 1.

units.zh: 時晉王方攻鎮州，故思遠乘虛以襲之，陷成安，而思遠遂急攻德勝北城，晉將李存審極力拒守。
units.en: While the Prince of Jin besieged Zhenzhou, Siyuan took Cheng'an and stormed Desheng’s north wall; Li Cunshen held firm.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Jin was attacking Zhenzhou; hence Siyuan seized the opening to strike, took Cheng'an, and then urgently attacked Desheng’s northern city; Jin commander Li Cunshen resisted with utmost strength.

units.zh: 二月，晉王以兵至，思遠收軍而退，復保楊村。
units.en: In the second month the Prince of Jin came up; Siyuan withdrew to Yang village.
units.literal: In the second month the Prince of Jin arrived with troops; Siyuan gathered the army and withdrew, again holding Yang village.

units.zh: 唐帝棄德勝之北城，並軍保楊劉。
units.en: The Tang emperor abandoned Desheng’s north wall and concentrated at Yangliu.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor abandoned Desheng’s northern city and combined the army to hold Yangliu.

units.zh: 六月乙亥，唐帝引軍援楊劉，潛軍至博州，築壘於河東岸。
units.en: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang emperor relieved Yangliu while secretly fortifying east of Bozhou.
units.literal: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang Emperor led troops to relieve Yangliu, secretly moving the army to Bozhou and building ramparts on the river’s east bank.

units.zh: 秋七月丁未，唐帝引軍沿河而南。
units.en: On dingwei in the seventh month the Tang emperor led his army south along the river.
units.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn the Tang Emperor led troops south along the river.

units.zh: 庚寅，唐帝軍於胡城，先鋒將康延孝率百騎奔於唐，盡泄其軍機。
units.en: On gengyin at Hucheng vanguard Kang Yanxiao defected with a hundred riders and betrayed Liang dispositions.
units.literal: On gengyin the Tang Emperor’s army was at Hucheng; vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led a hundred horsemen to defect to Tang and fully revealed our military plans.

units.zh: 甲戌，唐帝引師襲中都，王彥章兵潰，於是彥章與監軍張漢傑及趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、唐文通、王山興等皆為唐人所獲。
units.en: On jiaxu the Tang emperor stormed Zhongdu; Yanzhang’s army broke; he, Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, and others were taken.
units.literal: On jiaxu the Tang Emperor led troops to strike Zhongdu; Wang Yanzhang’s army collapsed; thereupon Yanzhang, army supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Tang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and others were all captured by Tang men.

units.zh: 帝置傳國寶於臥內，俄失其所在，已為左右所竊迎唐帝矣。
units.en: He laid the seal in his chamber; it vanished—courtiers had stolen it to greet the Tang emperor.
units.literal: The Emperor placed the dynastic seal in the sleeping chamber; soon it lost its place—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang Emperor.

units.zh: 唐帝入宮，妃郭氏號泣迎拜。
units.en: The Tang emperor entered the palace; Consort Guo wept and bowed in welcome.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor entered the palace; consort Guo wailed and came forward to bow.

units.zh: 唐帝初入東京，聞帝殂，憮然歎曰：「敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。
units.en: Entering the Eastern Capital, the Tang emperor learned of the Last Emperor’s death and sighed: "Grudges need not pass to sons.
units.literal: When the Tang Emperor first entered the Eastern Capital and heard the Emperor had died, he sighed in dejection: "Enemy kindness and enemy hatred do not lie in later generations.

units.zh: 九月庚寅，以供奉官郎公遠充契丹歡好使。
units.en: On gengyin in the ninth month Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was sent as envoy of goodwill to the Khitan.
units.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made Khitan Goodwill envoy.

units.zh: 龍德二年春正月，戴思遠率師襲魏州。
units.en: In the first month of Longde 2 Dai Siyuan raided Weizhou.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of Longde 2, Dai Siyuan led troops to raid Weizhou.

units.zh: 尋詔河南尹張全義收葬之，其首藏於太社。
units.en: He ordered Zhang Quanyi to bury the body; the head was kept at the Grand Altar.
units.literal: Soon an edict ordered Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi to collect and bury him; his head was stored at the Grand Altar.

units.zh: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下，晉王欲以嗣昭長子繼儔襲父位。
units.en: His father Li Sizhao had held Luzhou and died at Zhenzhou; the Prince of Jin meant to give the post to eldest son Jichou.
units.literal: Earlier, Jiyao’s father Sizhao was Luzhou military commissioner and fell in battle below Zhenzhou city; the Prince of Jin wished to let Sizhao’s eldest son Jichou succeed his father’s post.

units.zh: 朕與梁主十年對壘，恨不生見其面。」
units.en: We fought ten years; I regret never meeting him alive."
units.literal: I and the Liang ruler faced each other in battle ten years, regretting I did not see his face in life."

units.zh: 又，案《五代會要》所載，內職有梁太祖昭儀陳氏、昭容李氏，《歐陽史》並見《家人傳》。）〉
units.en: The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 also lists the Founder’s Lady of Bright Deportment Chen and Lady of Bright Countenance Li, both noted in Ouyang Xiu’s 《New History》 Family section.)〉
units.literal: Moreover, examining what the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records, among inner offices were the Founder’s Lady of Bright Deportment Chen and Lady of Bright Countenance Li; both appear in 《Ouyang’s History》 in the Family Biographies.)〉

units.zh: 案《歐陽史次妃郭氏傳》云：晉天福三年，詔太社先藏罪人首級，許親屬收葬，乃出末帝首，遣右衛將軍安崇阮與妃同葬。
units.en: Ouyang’s 《History》 biography of Consort Guo notes that in Tianfu 3 Jin permitted families to claim criminals’ heads from the Grand Altar; the Last Emperor’s head was released and General An Chongruan buried it with his consort.
units.literal: Examining 《Ouyang’s History》, in the biography of the second consort Guo it says: In Jin Tianfu year 3 an edict allowed kin to bury heads of criminals long stored at the Grand Altar; the Last Emperor’s head was produced, and Right Palace Guard general An Chongruan was sent to bury it together with the consort.

units.zh: 以天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為御營使。
units.en: Shi Jingtang of Tianxiong became imperial camp commissioner.
units.literal: Tianxiong army military commissioner Shi Jingtang was made imperial camp commissioner.

units.zh: 壬申，以成德軍節度行軍司馬、權知府事任圜為檢校右僕射、權北面水陸轉運製置使。
units.en: On renshen Ren Yuan, Chengde campaign marshal and acting prefect, became acting Right Vice Director and northern transport commissioner.
units.literal: On renshen, Chengde army campaign army marshal and acting prefect Ren Yuan was made acting Right Vice Director and acting northern land-and-water transport commissioner.

units.zh: 乙酉，前蔡州刺史董璋權知宣義軍軍州事。
units.en: On yiyou, Dong Zhang, former prefect of Cai, was given acting charge of Xuanyi Army affairs.
units.literal: On yiyou, former Cai prefect Dong Zhang was made acting Xuanyi Army military and prefectural commissioner.

units.zh: 二月甲申，晉王攻我黎陽，劉鄩拒之而退。
units.en: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked Liyang; Liu Xun held him off and forced a withdrawal.
units.literal: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked our Liyang; Liu Xun resisted him and drove him back.

units.zh: 貞明三年春正月戊午，以前淄州刺史高允奇為右羽林統軍。
units.en: On wuwu in the first month of Zhenming 3, Gao Yunqi, former Inspector of Zi Prefecture, was appointed commander of the Right Feathered Forest.
units.literal: On wuwu, in the first month of spring of Zhenming 3, former Zi Prefecture Inspector Gao Yunqi was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest.

units.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。
units.en: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

units.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。
units.en: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.
units.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
units.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
units.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
units.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

units.zh: 雄桀之士因勢輔時，作為權詐以相傾覆，吳有孫武，齊有孫臏，魏有吳起，秦有商鞅，皆禽敵立勝，垂著篇籍。
units.en: Strategists such as Sun Wu, Sun Bin, Wu Qi, and Shang Yang turned military thought toward power and deception, with influential textual legacies.
units.literal: Heroic and ruthless men, taking advantage of the age, made power techniques and deception to overturn one another: Wu had Sun Wu, Qi had Sun Bin, Wei had Wu Qi, Qin had Shang Yang-all captured enemies and secured victories, leaving written works.

units.zh: 世方爭於功利，而馳說者以孫、吳為宗。
units.en: With utility dominant, military discourse canonized the Sun-Wu tradition.
units.literal: As the age contended over profit and utility, persuasive theorists took Sun and Wu as their lineage.

units.zh: 時唯孫卿明於王道，而非之曰：「彼孫、吳者，上勢利而貴變詐；
units.en: Only Xunzi was clear on the kingly way and criticized them, saying: 'Those Sun and Wu strategists esteem advantage and prize changing deception;
units.literal: Only Xunzi was clear on the kingly way and criticized them, saying: 'Those Sun and Wu strategists esteem advantage and prize changing deception;

units.zh: 孫、吳、商、白之徒，皆身誅戮於前，而功滅亡於後。
units.en: The lineages of Sunzi, Wuzi, Shang Yang, and Bai Qi ended in violent ruin, and their victories did not endure.
units.literal: Followers of Sun, Wu, Shang, and Bai were all themselves executed in front, and their achievements perished afterward.

units.zh: 次均王友貞，為東都馬步都指揮使。
units.en: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, commander of horse and foot at the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, Eastern Capital Horse and Foot Commander.

units.zh: 遣供奉官丁昭溥馳詣東都，命均王友貞殺友文。
units.en: He sent palace attendant Ding Zhaopu in haste to the Eastern Capital to order Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.
units.literal: He dispatched Palace Attendant Ding Zhaopu posthaste to the Eastern Capital ordering Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.

units.zh: 梁祖在位止及六年，均帝朝詔史臣修梁祖實錄，岐下系鞋之事，恥而不書。
units.en: Taizu reigned only six years; under Emperor Jun historians were ordered to compile his veritable record—yet the shoe-tying at Qi was too shameful to write.
units.literal: Liang Taizu reigned only six years; in Emperor Jun’s reign an edict ordered historians to compile Taizu’s veritable record—the affair of tying shoes below Qi was shameful and not written.

units.zh: 辛巳，丁昭溥還，聞友文已死，乃發喪，宣遺制，友珪即皇帝位。
units.en: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; learning Youwen was dead, they announced mourning, proclaimed the testament, and Yougui seized the throne.
units.literal: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; hearing Youwen was already dead, they then announced the mourning, proclaimed the testamentary order, and Yougui at once took the throne.

units.zh: 戊辰，客省使李嚴使蜀回。
units.en: On wuchen Li Yan returned from Shu.
units.literal: On wuchen Guest Reception commissioner Li Yan returned from an embassy to Shu.

units.zh: 嚴不獲珍貨，歸而奏之，帝大怒曰：「物歸中夏者命之曰『入草』，王衍寧免為入草之人耶！」
units.en: Yan brought back no treasures and reported it; Cunxu thundered, "Goods that reach China are called 'entering grass'—is Wang Yan not a man who enters the grass!"
units.literal: Yan obtained no curios; on returning he memorialized this, and the Emperor raged: "Goods that reach the Central Realm are called 'entering grass'—can Wang Yan escape being a man who enters the grass!"

units.zh: 初，帝令往市蜀中珍玩，蜀法嚴峻，不許奇貨東出，其許市者謂之「入草物」。
units.en: Cunxu had sent him to buy Shu luxuries; Shu law barred rare goods from the east, allowing only what it called "entering-grass goods."
units.literal: Earlier the Emperor had ordered him to buy Shu curios; Shu law was severe and did not allow rare goods to leave eastward—what was permitted was called "entering-grass goods."
